body: I agree, this looks like a bug.

Also strange. When I feed the 'tied' covariance matrix into the 'full' log-density calculation with:

```
def _log_multivariate_normal_density_tied(X, means, covars):
    """Compute Gaussian log-density at X for a tied model"""
    cv = np.tile(covars,(means.shape[0],1,1))
    return _log_multivariate_normal_density_full(X, means, cv)
```

I get something more reasonable (and in better agreement with the Mclust results):
![test4](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/3067471/5584461/8116a2a8-9042-11e4-9bdb-af5a97943566.png)
but the 1 component BIC scores are still not exactly the same. I tried dropping the thresh=1e-6 and upping n_iter=1000, but it didn't seem to make any difference. I also made the plot with 'full' instead of 'diag' and got the same result. This makes me think that it is related to the mean and covariance optimization routines (perhaps different for 'tied' vs the other methods).

The discrepancy noted in the previous comment appears to be due to a error in the following function:

```
def _covar_mstep_tied(gmm, X, responsibilities, weighted_X_sum, norm,
                      min_covar):
    # Eq. 15 from K. Murphy, "Fitting a Conditional Linear Gaussian
    n_features = X.shape[1]
    avg_X2 = np.dot(X.T, X)
    avg_means2 = np.dot(gmm.means_.T, weighted_X_sum)
    return (avg_X2 - avg_means2 + min_covar * np.eye(n_features)) / X.shape[0]
```

I think the return line should read:

```
return (avg_X2 - avg_means2) / X.shape[0] + min_covar * np.eye(n_features) 
```

When this correction is made there is agreement between the BIC scores:
![test7](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/3067471/5584628/0372ce70-9048-11e4-917f-d21ca8ab1c32.png)

I want to go through the code one more time and compare with  K. Murphy, "Fitting a Conditional Linear Gaussian Distribution" to make sure that this is correct and not two mistakes canceling out one another before I make pull request.

Thank you for digging into this!
If you feel confident enough to make a PR, please add a non-regression tests that scores agree for the 1d case.

I am new to contributing to scikit-learn so would you mind going into a bit more detail about what you want in the NRT. And do you want me to commit the NRT, if so where? (I have read the contributing guidelines)

> For 1 dimensional data fit with a one component GMM, I would expect that the BIC scores of the 'tied' and other covariance types ('diag', 'spherical', 'full') should be the same
> 
> > a bit more detail about what you want in the NRT

You could assert the similarity of BIC "scores of the 'tied' and other covariance types ('diag', 'spherical', 'full')" in the test. Please look at the below file for existing tests.

> And do you want me to commit the NRT, if so where? 

The NRT should be added to [this file](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/master/sklearn/mixture/tests/test_gmm.py)

Thanks for trying to fix this issue :)

issue.title: Corrected two bugs related to 'tied' covariance_type in mixture.GMM(), a...
issue.body:
...dded test, closes #4036

The first bug was with the Gaussian log-density calculation for the 'tied' covariance_type.
Rather than fix this equation I reformatted the covars data structure so that it could be fed
into the 'full' covariance_type log-density calculation. It might be a tiny bit slower but I think
it is better to have the least amount of potentially redundant code as this should minimize
the potential for such errors.

The second bug I fixed was related to the _covar_mstep_tied() function, only the first part
of the equation should be divided by X.shape[0].

body: Note that I have verified these GMM() fixes in commit ea033dc against Mclust BIC scores for the same non-trivial 1D data.

issue.title: [RFC] GSoC2015 Improve GMM API
issue.body:
GSoC 2015 project,  Improve GMM API
1. [x] Completes [derivation report](https://www.dropbox.com/s/8hlbb7dlwllwcry/VBGMM.pdf?dl=0).
2. [x] Adds new classes. One abstract class `_BasesMixture`. Three derived classes `GaussianMixture`, `BayesianGaussianMixture`, `DirichletProcessGaussianMixture`
3. [x] Decouples large functions, especially in `DirichletProcessGaussianMixture` and `BayesianGaussianMixture`
4. [x] Removes numerical stability fixes for HMM. It seems that whenever there is a numerical issue, the code always adds 10_EPS in the computation. I think in some cases there is a better way to address the problem, such as normalization the extremely small variables earlier, or we just simply remove ```10_EPS``` which is only for HMM.
5. [x] Writes updating functions for `BayesianGaussianMixtureModel` and `DirichletProcessGaussianMixtureModel` according to the report.
6. [x] Provides methods that allow users to initialize the model with user-provided data
7. [x] Corrects kmeans initialization. It is weird when using kmeans initialization, only means is initialized. The weights and covariances are initialized by averaging.
8. [x] Writes several checking functions for the initialization data
9. [x] Adjusts the verbose messages. When `verbose>1`, it display log-likelihood and time used in the same line of the message `Iteration x`
10. [x] Remove `fit_predict`
11. [x] Adds warning for `params!='wmc'`
12. [ ] Studies and contrasts the convergence of classical MLE / EM GMM with Bayesian GMM against the number of samples and the number of components
13. [x] Friendly warning and error messages, or automatically addressing if possible (e.g. random re-init of singular components)
14. [ ] Examples that shows how models can over-fit by comparing likelihood on training and validation sets (normalized by
    the number of samples). For instance extend the BIC score example with a cross-validated likelihood plot
15. [x] Testing on 1-D dimensions
16. [x] Testing on Degenerating cases
17. [optional] add a partial_fit function for incremental / out-of-core fitting of (classical) GMM, for instance http://arxiv.org/abs/0712.4273 
18. [optional] ledoit_wolf covariance estimation or `PCA(n_components).fit(X_train).get_covariance()`
